slides.title: CAST in four steps: animated Figure 2.
slides.narration: Here’s one learning step. We first sample paired actions. Next, the critic proposes an improvement. We normalize, cap, and scale its gradient. We also pull toward the base, with a stronger pull beyond the reference radius. We combine these arrows and cap the target step around the current action. We then fit the correction to these fixed targets, and repeat the process.

slides.title: Reach useful performance with less experience.
slides.narration: The measured results show the same pattern. In robomimic square, CAST reaches ninety percent success using thirty-eight percent fewer environment steps than DICE-RL. Across five LIBERO tasks, no controls or clipping alone gives zero success, while CAST improves every task over the base.
